To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the joint allocation power and the channel can significantly enlarge the achievable rate regions for orthogonal multiple access relaying systems and that the problem can often be formulated as a convex optimization problem, thus admitting efficient algorithms to obtain the jointly power and resource allocation.
the problem of joint resource and power allocation for orthogonal MAR systems can be formulated as quasiconvext problems and efficient algorithms can be designed to solve the quasiconvexe problems.

joint power and channel allocation can achieve a much higher achievable rate region than power allocation alone, with the channel resource fixed, and that assigning different relays to different users together and joint allocation of power can further enlarge the rate region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of jointly optimizing the power and channel resource for MAR systems with multiple users and multiple relays.
the joint allocation problem of power, channel resource, and relaying strategies for orthogonal MAR systems.
the joint power and channel allocation in orthogonal multiple access relay systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the joint allocation outperforms power allocation alone with channel resource allocation fixed and the joint allocation together with the different relaying strategies outperforms the joint allocation with the same relaying strategy.
the joint optimization of the power and the channel allocation is a very powerful tool to enlarge the achievable rate regions in MAR systems.
the joint optimization of power and channel resource is a very important issue in MAR systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
joint power and resource allocation for orthogonal MAR systems can be efficiently performed and that the achievable rate regions are significantly enlarged by the joint allocation of resources.
joint power and channel allocation is necessary to achieve the maximum possible achievable rate region for orthogonal multiple access systems.
we have shown that the joint allocation power and the channel is optimal in the sense of achieving a maximum achievable rate region, and we have also demonstrated how to achieve this maximum.

the joint power and channel allocation is an important aspect for the design of orthogonal MAR systems.

the jointly optimal power allocation and channel resource allocation can achieve significantly larger rate regions than the power allocation alone with the fixed channel resource allocation, especially when the channel resource allocation is optimized for the direct channel.
the joint power and channel allocation can significantly enlarge the achievable rate regions of MAR systems.
